info.name: Identity System API v1
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for testing all Identity System API endpoints.

## Authentication
Most endpoints require JWT Bearer authentication. Use the Login endpoint first to obtain tokens.

## Variables
- `baseUrl`: API base URL (default: http://localhost:5000)
- `accessToken`: JWT access token (auto-set after login)
- `refreshToken`: Refresh token (auto-set after login)
- `userId`: Current user ID (auto-set after login)

## Argon2id Hashing
All secrets, tokens, and API keys are hashed using Argon2id algorithm.

exec: // Auto-refresh access token before it expires (sliding expiration)
// Skip for auth endpoints (login, register, refresh) to avoid loops
// Check if token expires within 2 minutes
console.log('Access token expires in ' + remainingSeconds + 's — auto-refreshing...');
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ refreshToken: refreshToken }) }
// Fallback: if 401 received, try to refresh so the next request works
// Skip for auth endpoints to avoid loops
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ refreshToken: refreshToken }) }
// Auto-capture X-New-Access-Token header (for future server-side sliding expiration)
console.log('Access token updated from X-New-Access-Token header.');

Returns the current status of all managed secrets (RSA keys, HMAC keys, gateway token). Does not expose secret values.

Step 1 of every destructive key operation. Emails a one-time code to the calling administrator and returns { challengeId, expiresAt, maskedEmail }. Nothing is rotated here. operation is one of GenerateRsaKey, GenerateHmacKey, GenerateGatewayToken, ImportRsaKey, ImportHmacKey, ImportGatewayToken. For the import operations also send "value" with the key material: the confirmation is bound to a digest of it, so the approved bytes are the only bytes that can be installed.

Step 2. Accepts the emailed code and returns the operation's blast radius (affected users plus the per-consequence counts) together with approvalExpiresAt. The approval is spendable for five minutes. Every failure shape returns the same Secret.InvalidChallengeCode; five wrong attempts burn the challenge.

Step 3. Generates a new RSA key pair used for JWT signing. Requires a verified confirmation raised for this exact operation; the approval is spent on use, so a replay returns 403 Secret.ChallengeNotApproved. Takes effect for users only after the API process restarts.

Step 3. Generates a new HMAC key. Requires a verified confirmation raised for this exact operation. This one key also hashes password-reset links, two-factor challenges and webhook keys, so rotating it breaks all four.

Step 3. Generates a new gateway authentication token. Requires a verified confirmation raised for this exact operation. Invalidates no user credential, but the API rejects all proxied traffic until the gateway carries the same value.

Imports a caller-supplied RSA private key (PKCS#8 or PKCS#1 PEM, at least 2048-bit). Certificate or Dpapi mode only (returns 409 in PlainText). Requires a verified confirmation raised for ImportRsaKey with this byte-identical value; submitting different material returns 403 Secret.ChallengeNotApproved. Replaces the JWT signing key and invalidates existing access tokens. Set importRsaPrivateKeyPem to the PEM with line breaks escaped.

Imports a caller-supplied HMAC key (Base64, at least 32 bytes). Certificate or Dpapi mode only (returns 409 in PlainText). Requires a verified confirmation raised for ImportHmacKey with this byte-identical value. Replaces the refresh-token HMAC key and invalidates existing refresh tokens, password-reset links, two-factor challenges and webhook keys.

Imports a caller-supplied gateway token (at least 16 characters). Certificate or Dpapi mode only (returns 409 in PlainText). Requires a verified confirmation raised for ImportGatewayToken with this byte-identical value. The API Gateway must be reconfigured with the same token.
